heroText: Roskilde is a historic Zealand city known for royal burials, Viking ships and one of Europe's major music festivals. Start at Roskilde Cathedral, walk down to the Viking Ship Museum, then use Roskilde Fjord or Musicon to see the city's newer side. Copenhagen Airport is the main international gateway, with easy rail onward.

areas.name: Roskilde centre
areas.text: The centre is best for first stays, with the cathedral, station, shops and restaurants within easy walking distance.

areas.name: Harbour area
areas.text: The harbour area suits fjord views, Viking Ship Museum visits and quieter walks below the old centre.

areas.name: Musicon
areas.text: Musicon is Roskilde's creative district, useful for festival energy, events and a less traditional stay.

areas.name: Trekroner
areas.text: Trekroner is a newer residential and university area with rail access east of the historic centre.

airports.name: Copenhagen Airport (CPH)
airports.text: Copenhagen Airport is the main international airport for Roskilde, connected by rail through Copenhagen.

airportTransfer.value: 45-60 min by train from Copenhagen Airport via Copenhagen

stayOverview: Stay in Roskilde centre for the station, cathedral and restaurants, the harbour area for fjord walks, Musicon for events and festival atmosphere, or Trekroner for university access and newer apartment stays.
hotelIntro: Roskilde is easy to cover on foot from the station and centre. Harbour stays feel quieter and scenic, while Musicon is more event-led and Trekroner works when rail access or university visits matter.
rentalCars: A car is not needed in Roskilde, but helps for fjord villages, Ledreborg and countryside stops.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the centre if you want the cathedral, station and restaurants close together without relying on buses.

travelTips.title: Festival dates
travelTips.text: Keep the Roskilde plan compact: group nearby sights together and leave enough time for transfers, meals and weather changes.

travelTips.title: Fjord walks
travelTips.text: Leave time to walk between the cathedral area and the Viking Ship Museum by the fjord.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Roskilde also works as a day trip from Copenhagen if you only need the cathedral and Viking ships.

history.label: 11th century
history.text: From the 11th century until 1443, it was the capital of Denmark.
It is unclear when Roskilde became a market town but it was certainly enjoying trading privileges under King Eric II who reigned from 1134 to 1137.
In 1135 the town was destroyed by the Pomeranian duke Ratibor I.
In 1150, Sweyn Grathe built a moat around the city.
In 1151/2, a religious confraternity was founded for the defence of the town against Wendish pirates.
Absalon, the Danish bishop, had a brick church built on the site of Harald's church in 1170.
The Roskilde bishops owned large areas of land in the region including, from 1186, Havn on the Øresund which later became Copenhagen.
These privileges were firmly established when the Roskilde City Council granted market town status to other towns on Zealand on 15 June 1268.
Today's cathedral was completed in 1275 after five of Absalon's successors had contributed to its construction.
Conditions improved in 1835 when the city became the Assembly of the Estates of the Realm (Rådgivende Stænderforsamling) and in 1847 with the railway connecting Copenhagen and Roskilde.

history.label: 1970s
history.text: In the 1970s, the city benefited from the Holbæk Motorway which linked it to Copenhagen and the establishment of Roskilde University in 1972.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: By the Middle Ages, with the support of kings and bishops, it had become one of the most important centres in Scandinavia.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: As a result of Absalon's influence, many other churches were built in the vicinity, making Roskilde the most important town in Zealand.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: With the development of the rail network, Roskilde became an important hub for traffic with Copenhagen.
